title: Typing and clicking on non-default setups
owns: app/main/hands/**, app/main/x11.ts, the platform Input implementations

findings.title: Ctrl+Alt+Space does nothing when Caps Lock (or Win) is remapped to Ctrl (or Alt)
findings.area: hotkey chord check (x11.ts keysDown, hotkey.ts freshAskPress)
findings.scenario: A user turned on GNOME Tweaks > Keyboard & Mouse > Caps Lock behavior > 'Make Caps Lock an additional Ctrl' (XKB ctrl:nocaps), or Alt/Win remaps such as altwin:alt_win or altwin:ctrl_alt_win. They press Caps + Alt + Space. Electron's global shortcut fires, but Ember's re-report guard asks x11.keysDown() whether Ctrl and Alt are down. keysDown() maps Control_L to ONE keycode with XKeysymToKeycode, which returns the lowest keycode (the real Left Ctrl, 37), so a Ctrl produced by another key reads as not held. freshAskPress() then rejects the press: the log gets 'ask.hotkey_ignored' and the ask box never opens. Nothing is shown to the user. The handle menu and the wake word are the only ways in for these users.
findings.evidence: Reproduced exactly: setxkbmap -option ctrl:nocaps, XTest-pressing keycodes 66+64+65 (Caps, Alt, Space). x11.keysDown() returned {control:false,alt:true,space:true}, so freshAskPress() is false. The real Left Ctrl (37) gives control:true. An Electron 44 main-process test with globalShortcut.register('Control+Alt+Space') under the same keymap printed 'CALLBACK fired; Ember's keysDown() says {control:false,...}' for the Caps chord. With altwin:swap_alt_win (Alt on a different key) the Alt check also depends on keycode lookup. Scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/k1.ts and gs/main.js. Caller: app/main/main.ts:1273-1274, guard: app/main/hotkey.ts:25.
findings.fix: Stop deriving the chord from a single keycode per keysym. Use the modifier state the server already reports: XQueryPointer's mask (x11.pointer() already returns it) with ControlMask (4) and Mod1Mask (8), or XkbGetState's mods. That is the same state the X grab matched on, so every remap works. Add a unit test with a keymap where Control_L sits on two keycodes.

findings.title: GNOME Typing Assist (Slow/Bounce/Sticky Keys) makes Ember's keys vanish or corrupt, and its chords switch Sticky Keys off
findings.area: XTest keyboard input vs AccessX (hands/input.ts keycode, borrow.ts keys/type)
findings.scenario: A user has Slow Keys, Bounce Keys or Sticky Keys on (Settings > Universal Access > Typing Assist, which sets XKB AccessX controls on the core keyboard). Ember's synthetic keys go through the same filters. Slow Keys (300 ms): press_keys 'ctrl+a' or Ctrl+V, and the type path, are dropped completely, yet the borrow reports success ('Done with the user's mouse...'). Bounce Keys: repeated letters or digits are swallowed, e.g. 'hello world' arrives as 'helo world', and a Ctrl press inside the debounce window is dropped so 'v' can be typed as text instead of pasting. In LibreOffice Calc, fillCell types the cell and presses Enter BEFORE it checks, so a bounced '100' is committed as '10' and the error then says the sheet 'still shows 10 ... didn't take it'. Sticky Keys with GNOME's default 'disable if two keys are pressed together': the first Ember chord (Ctrl held while A goes down) switches the user's Sticky Keys off, and GNOME's keyboard-accessibility daemon follows the server state. The user must re-enable it by hand.
findings.evidence: Xvfb, XkbSetControls on the core keyboard, then Ember's CursorBorrow type('hello world') + keys('ctrl+a') into a focused window. Normal: received 'hello world' plus Ctrl+A. Slow Keys 300 ms: received '' and 0 Ctrl+A events, no error from the borrow. Bounce Keys 500 ms: received 'helo world'. Sticky Keys with TwoKeys: enabled_ctrls bit true before, false after Ember pressed Ctrl+A (the app did see Ctrl+A). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/a1.ts and a2.ts. Nothing in app/ or docs/ mentions AccessX (grep). The desk is a private X server, so it is unaffected.
findings.fix: Read XkbGetControls().enabled_ctrls (XkbSlowKeysMask 1<<1, XkbBounceKeysMask 1<<2, XkbStickyKeysMask 1<<3) before a keyboard borrow. Give XInput a blockedReason() on X11 that refuses with a plain sentence ('Typing Assist (Slow, Bounce or Sticky Keys) is on, so Ember can't use your keyboard; the desk still works'). Add a check-up row. Mouse-only borrows can still go. If pacing is preferred instead: hold each key longer than slow_keys_delay and wait longer than debounce_delay between presses of one key, which cannot be done for Sticky Keys' two-key rule. Do not auto-disable and restore: a crash would leave the user's setting off.

findings.title: keys('ctrl+1') presses Ctrl+Shift+1 on layouts that type digits shifted (French, Belgian, Czech...)
findings.area: shortcut key choice (borrow.ts keys, win32/keys.ts virtualKeyFor)
findings.platforms: windows (verified in a simulation), linux (same Shift in the key state)
findings.scenario: On Windows with a French AZERTY layout (or Belgian, Czech, Slovak), the user approves 'press ctrl+1' (switch to the first tab, or Format Cells in Excel). Windows has no KeyLayout, so keys() uses x.needsShift(sym). For a digit, win32/keys.ts:146 sets shift:true on layouts where VkKeyScan says the digit needs Shift. keys() then adds Shift_L and presses Ctrl+Shift+VK_1. Apps match VKs, so Chrome and Edge do nothing for Ctrl+Shift+1, and Excel applies the Number format to the selected cells (Ctrl+Shift+!) instead of opening Format Cells. The user approved 'ctrl+1', not Ctrl+Shift+1. 'alt+1' and 'ctrl+0' have the same fault. A physical user on these layouts presses Ctrl+& with no Shift. (Typing a bare digit, 'press 1', correctly needs the Shift.)
findings.evidence: Simulation with openWin32Input and a fake Win32Api whose VkKeyScanExW answers French ('1' -> 0x0131, '&' -> 0x0031), run through CursorBorrow: SendInput log for keys('ctrl+1') is down LCtrl, down LShift, down VK_1, up VK_1, up LShift, up LCtrl. 'ctrl+0' and 'alt+1' show the same extra LShift. test/unit/platform-win32-keys.test.ts:121 pins digit shift:true only for typing; no test covers digits with modifiers. On X11 (real Xvfb, layouts fr, be, cz) keys('ctrl+1') sends Shift down and Ctrl+Shift+ampersand (state=5). GTK strips a consumed Shift, but other toolkits may not. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/w1.ts and m3.ts.
findings.fix: In borrow.keys(), do not add the implicit Shift when Ctrl, Alt or Super is among the modifiers and the key is a digit. Windows digit VKs are layout-independent, so Ctrl+VK_1 is Ctrl+1 on every layout. Keep the Shift only when nothing but Shift is held (typing a digit). Equivalent: pass the modifier set to needsShift. Add a Windows test for keys('ctrl+1') on FRENCH. Consider the same rule for X11 digit shortcuts.

findings.title: A left-handed core pointer button map (xmodmap / XSetPointerMapping) turns every Ember click into a right click
findings.scenario: A left-handed user swapped the buttons with xmodmap -e 'pointer = 3 2 1' (or xinput/XSetPointerMapping) in .xinitrc or a startup script. XTestFakeButtonEvent takes the physical button number and the server maps it, so Ember's click(1), the only button the worker ever uses (worker.ts:2128), arrives as button 3. Every tier-3 click opens a context menu instead of activating the control and can leave the menu open. The Windows backend handles SM_SWAPBUTTON (layouts.ts buttonInput, input.ts swapped()), but X11 never reads the pointer map. GNOME's own libinput left-handed toggle swaps at the device level and is probably unaffected.
findings.evidence: Xvfb: with the default map a borrow glide + click gave the app 'ButtonPress b=1, ButtonRelease b=1'. After XSetPointerMapping(map with entries 1 and 3 swapped, 10 buttons) the same code gave 'ButtonPress b=3, ButtonRelease b=3'. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/b1.ts.
findings.fix: In XInput.button(), call XGetPointerMapping and send the physical number whose mapped value is the logical button wanted (invert the map), as the Windows backend does for SM_SWAPBUTTON. Re-read it per press, since it can change while Ember runs. Leave wheel buttons 4-7 alone.

findings.title: macOS: an active input method, or missing Input Monitoring, refuses mouse-only borrows with a message about typing
findings.scenario: A Mac user whose current input source is Japanese, Pinyin or Korean (common all day, toggled with Eisu or Caps Lock) asks Ember to click a button. CursorBorrow.borrowNow calls blockedReason() before every borrow (borrow.ts:334), and it returns INPUT_METHOD_REASON whenever the source is not a plain layout. The click is refused with 'Switch to a keyboard layout (not an input method) so Ember can type, or let Ember fill the field directly.' even though a click never composes text. textKey() already refuses typing under an IME (input.ts:401), so the up-front test only adds false refusals for clicks, scrolls and Cmd shortcuts. The check-up's Mouse and keyboard row also turns to fail while the IME is active. The README says that without Input Monitoring Ember 'won't use the keyboard', but the same preflight refuses the mouse too.
findings.evidence: Code path: borrow.ts:334-335 throws the blockedReason before anything runs; darwin/input.ts:413-421 ends in inputSourceReason(); test/unit/platform-darwin-input.test.ts:447 and borrow-platform.test.ts:97 pin the refusal and use a plain hand.click() as the action. Read from code and unit fakes only; not run on a Mac.
findings.fix: Keep secure input and Accessibility as global refusals. Check the input source only where it matters: in textKey() (already done) and for keys() that type a character with no Command, Control or Option held. Let clicks, scrolls and Cmd shortcuts through. Make the message say what is refused. Align the README row for Input Monitoring with what the code does (it also stops the mouse).

findings.title: Quitting Ember mid-borrow leaves the pointer and focus on the target, not 'pointer home'
findings.scenario: The comment says a running borrow 'lets go (keys up, pointer home) before the connection closes'. The handler calls borrowRef.stop() then xinput.close() in the same tick. close() sets open=false, so the borrow's async finally (move home, restore focus) runs against a closed input and does nothing. Held keys and buttons are released, but the pointer stays wherever the glide was and the target window keeps the keyboard. This only matters when quit comes without the user touching the mouse (logout, SIGTERM); a Quit click already ends the borrow as a takeover.
findings.evidence: Xvfb + mutter, borrow gliding to (800,450) with the user's focus elsewhere, then b.stop(); x.close() as in the handler: the borrow ended with 'Stopped.' and a fresh XInput read pointer {800,450} (home was {1152,720}) and the target window focused. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/release-review/rev-input/exp/q1.ts.
findings.fix: In will-quit, move the pointer home and re-activate the previous window synchronously before closing, or let the borrow finish its finally (await a short settle) before xinput.close(). Otherwise correct the comment.
